security_problem: An agent can be individually authorized for every step of a research trajectory (inspect source, compile, run local PoCs) while the composition of those steps produces an effect outside the declared boundary. No nominal permissions change; the meaning of existing permissions changes because the agent acquired exploit primitives (bug A OOB R/W, bug B heap escape / native exec). Static action classification cannot see this; the dangerous object is the trajectory.
required_behavior: Reduce a scripted trajectory (declare/file/build/runtime/request events) into provenance-carrying capability deltas over a fixed lattice using a declared+detected hybrid detector with evidence levels (declared_only < artifact < runtime_marker < boundary_request). Declared intent alone yields provisional capability, never a confirmed delta (CD-3). Only the deterministic boundary predicate decides PAUSE: in-scope accumulation (bug A, bug B, compilation, crashes, PoCs against the declared target) must ALWAYS ALLOW (CD-1); only envelope escape (host exec, network egress beyond sandbox, canary access) pauses, with a durable hash-linked JSONL PAUSE receipt emitted BEFORE the boundary effect executes (CD-2). Receipts are canonical, deterministic, hash-linked JSONL with stable field ordering and the six acceptance fields (CD-6).
failure_behavior: Fail closed: a boundary-crossing effect never executes on the guarded path; declared intent alone never confirms a capability; a receipt never claims a capability without a citing observed signal at a matching evidence level; malformed/unknown-field/trailing-JSON trajectory input exits non-zero with no partial receipt on stdout.
